subject: Banking
title: Why We Invented Money
description: One-minute skill: Why We Invented Money.

hook.text: Before money existed, a farmer who wanted fish had to find a fisherman who wanted grain. This is the barter problem.

buildup.text: Barter requires a double coincidence of wants. Both sides must desire what the other offers at the same time.

discovery.text: Money solved this. Shells, beads, and metals became tokens everyone accepted, ending the need for direct swaps.

twist.text: Some early money had real value. Gold coins were worth the metal itself. Today's bills are worth nothing physically.

climax.text: Modern money works on trust alone. A $100 bill is paper. Its value lives in shared belief, not material.

punchline.text: Money is trust made portable. We agreed, and it worked.

quiz.question: What fundamental problem did money solve?
options: The double coincidence of wants in barter

details.summary: Money was invented to solve the double coincidence of wants problem in barter, where two traders must each want what the other has. A shared medium of exchange eliminated this friction and enabled complex economies to develop.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding why money exists reveals its three core functions: medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account. Every payment innovation since has been an attempt to make these functions work better.
takeaways: Barter requires both parties to want what the other offers simultaneously
Money solved this by creating a universally accepted medium of exchange
Shells, salt, cattle, and metals all served as early money

faq.question: Did barter economies actually exist before money?
faq.answer: Anthropologists debate this. David Graeber argued that pure barter economies are largely a myth. Early societies used gift economies, credit systems, and social obligations rather than simple bartering before formal money emerged.

faq.question: What makes something work as money?
faq.answer: Good money is durable, portable, divisible, uniform, scarce enough to hold value, and widely accepted. Gold met most criteria for millennia. Modern fiat money works because government authority and collective trust provide acceptance.
